transcript.message: Hi, I'm Angela. I'm a licensed mental health counselor. We talked briefly on the phone last week and I'm really glad that you are able to come to today's appointment.
Hi Angela, I'm James Knight. Thanks for seeing me today. I guess I'm here because things have been pretty up and down for me lately.

Yes, I remember from our conversation that your life has been really challenging lately. Before we get started, I just want to make sure you know about a few confidentiality guidelines. Your information that you share with me is private. If we are going to bill your insurance, I will need to give them some basic information about your diagnoses and treatment plan. The other exceptions to confidentiality would be if you were to tell me that you are going to harm or kill yourself or someone else. Or if you let me know about a child, elder or person who is disabled being abused. Does all of that make sense from your perspective?
Yeah, that makes sense. I appreciate you going over that. I've had experiences where I've felt misunderstood or my feelings were minimized, so it's important to me that things are clear between us.
Yes, I agree. It's important that you feel like this can be a place for you to be open about your thoughts and feelings, and that you can feel understood.
I hope so. It's been tough lately with all these intense mood swings and feeling kind of empty. It's hard when I feel like people just don't get it.
Is it ok with you if I ask you some questions to see if I can better understand what you are going through?
Sure, that's fine. What do you want to know?
Can you describe the mood swings to me? Like what seems to set them off and how long they last?

They can change really quickly. Sometimes it's stuff like feeling ignored or dismissed by someone close to me. I can feel really sad or angry, like everything's crashing down, and it can last hours or even all day.

Ok, yes, I can see how feeling ignored or dismissed would lead you to feel sad or angry. And it sounds like it's sometimes long lasting and sometimes goes on for shorter periods of time. When you say you feel empty, can you tell me more about that feeling?
It’s like there’s nothing there, no purpose or direction. Just this void. It gets overwhelming and hard to shake off.
That sounds like a terrible feeling
Yeah, it really is. It's frustrating and makes everything feel pointless.
Do you struggle with feeling like you should end your life or harm yourself?
I don't feel that way right now. I've struggled with it in the past, but not currently.
Do you remember the last time you felt like killing yourself?
It was a while ago. Things have been rough, but not to that point lately.
Got it. How about wanting to harm yourself in some way that wouldn't kill you, though would cause you bodily harm?
No, I haven't felt that urge lately either.
Ok, thanks for clarifying that. Can you tell me more about your close relationships?
They've been pretty rocky. I seem to idealize people one moment and get really upset with them the next. It makes things hard to keep stable.
Yes, I know what you mean. So sometimes you can feel really good about someone and then something happens where you ten feel really badly about them?
Exactly, it's like a switch flips. It feels out of my control sometimes.
Right, I bet it does.  Do you feel worried about  being rejected or abandoned by people?
Yeah, a lot. It's like I'm always on edge, worrying that people will leave or forget about me.
That can cause a lot of suffering
It really does. It tends to make everything else feel even more unstable.
When you talk about feeling unstable, do you feel like that extends to your identity within yourself too? Like you don't fully know who you are as a person?
Yeah, sometimes I feel like I don't really know myself or where I fit in. It's like everything is shifting around inside.
Yes, I talk with other people who describe that same kind of feeling. Do you struggle with impulsivity in your life like with spending money or sex or anything like that?
I have in the past. I try to keep it in check, but when emotions are high, it can be hard to manage.
Right, when emotions feel out of control, sometimes people turn to things that aren't as healthy
Exactly. It's like looking for any way to feel better, even if it doesn't really help in the long run.
Back to emotions, when you are having the mood swings, do you ever feel like anger is difficult ti manage or control?
Definitely. Anger can be intense, and it's hard to keep it in check, especially when I feel misunderstood.
Yes, I think that anger can be an underdstandable emotion in reaction to feeling misunderstood.  Do you ever have periods of feeling paranoid, like especially when stress is high?
Yeah, sometimes I worry that people are talking about me or plotting against me, especially when things get stressful.
Got it. Yes, I can see how that can happen. How about this symptom - do you ever feel like your body is here but your mind is someplace else? We refer to it as "dissociation"
Yeah, I've had moments like that, especially when things feel really overwhelming. It's like I'm not fully present.
Yes, makes sense. When you are feeling desperate to feel better, do you ever turn to alcohol or drugs in an effort to feel differently?
I used to in my younger days, but not so much now. I try to avoid it.
That's great, what a good decision you are making for yourself.  Sounds like you try to avoid it as much as possible. How often would you say you use alcohol or drugs?
These days, not often at all. I might have a drink occasionally, but I try to keep it in moderation.
Ok, so not a current issue. Would you say that you are having trouble with anxiety?
Yeah, anxiety is definitely something I struggle with, especially around relationships and work stuff.
Is it to the extent that you are not able to function at work?
It makes things difficult sometimes, but I’m still managing to get my work done.

Ok, so it's there, though so far you have been able to continue on with work. And I can appreciate how you would feel anxious around relationships given what you shared earlier about what happens in your relationships.
Yeah, it all seems connected. It just feels like I'm constantly juggling everything and hoping it won't all fall apart.
Just a few more questions about symptoms to make sure I'm not missing anything. Have you been through traumatic events in your lifetime?
Yeah, I've had some tough experiences growing up, especially with my family situation.
Do you find yourself continuing to re-live some of those experiences?
Sometimes memories come back, especially when things get stressful. They can feel pretty vivid.
Sounds really stressful. Do you find yourself actively trying to avoid remembering stressful events?
Yeah, I try not to think about them, but it doesn't always work. They creep in anyway.
How about this - do you notice that your nervous system gets "revved up" and it's difficult to calm yourself? This may interfere with sleep or concentration
Definitely. I often feel on edge, and it makes it hard to relax or focus, especially when I’m stressed.

Ok. I think you've done a really great job today answering a lot of questions and helping me to understand what you are struggling with.  I believe that there are some treatment approaches that we can work with to help reduce these symptoms and your suffering. It will involve meeting regularly and a willingness on your part to do some between session work. What do you think about this?
I appreciate you saying that. I'm willing to try, but I'm a bit nervous about how it will all go. I've had experiences before that didn't always feel helpful.

Yes, I'm hopeful that we can keep open communication so that you can let me know when something is not feeling helpful or you are struggling in some way with our work. I will rely on you for this feedback because I won't be able to automatically know what is happening for you internally
I can do that. I'll try to be open so we can make this work. I just hope things can finally start feeling a little more stable.
Yes, I hear that stability is a major goal that you have - with your emotions, your sense of self and your relationships
Exactly. It would mean a lot to feel like things aren't constantly in chaos.

Right, most people can't really thrive in constant chaos. Ok, so let's wrap up for today and if you're willing, it would be great if you could spend some time between now and next week writing out some goals in your own words for what you want to see different in your life and then we can create a plan
That sounds doable. I'll give it a shot and see what I can come up with. See you next week, then?
Yes, see you next week.
Alright, take care until then.

transcript.message: Hello Jame my name is Maria Rodriguez Nunez I will be your nurse practioner student
Hi Maria, nice to meet you. Thanks for taking the time to see me today.

Of course! Before we get started, I just wanted to explain this telehealth visit, we will discuss why you are here and move forward with a plan that feels the best for you. this visit should take aporoxiek aelty 20mintues is that ok with you/
Yeah, that sounds fine to me. I'm just hoping to get a better handle on what's been going on with me lately.
I hear you. As we begin can you verifry your name and date of birth
Sure, my name is James Knight, and my date of birth is May 12, 1966.
Ok thank you for that. Can you now explain to me what bring you here today

Lately, I've been having these intense mood swings and feeling really empty. It's like any small thing can trigger me into feeling like I'm on an emotional roller coaster. I also feel really distressed when it seems like people are abandoning or invalidating me, whether they're close to me or not. It's just been really hard to manage.
I can tell you that you are not alone and I am hear to listen
Thank you, I appreciate that. It's been tough, and it means a lot to hear that.
Can you tell me more on when this began?
Well, it's been going on for several years now. I can't pinpoint an exact time it started, but it's definitely gotten worse recently with some stress at work and in my personal life.
Can you tell me why it has recently gotten worse?

I've been dealing with a lot of instability at work since I'm freelancing, which has been stressful. On top of that, my personal relationships haven't been very stable, either. It all just feels overwhelming.
It sounds like you have alot on your plate but there are resources I can provide if you are interested later in this visit.
I guess that could be helpful. Sometimes it feels like any bit of support might make a difference.
I understand that. Have you felt things have been piling up for you?
Yeah, that's exactly how it feels. Like everything is just stacking up and I'm constantly trying to keep it from collapsing.
Have you felt any thoughts of hurting others or yourself?
I don't have any thoughts of hurting myself or others right now. In the past, I've had some self-harming behaviors, but I'm trying to stay away from that.
Can you tell me more about that?

I used to hurt myself during my late teens when things felt overwhelming and I didn't know how else to cope. It hasn't happened in years, but the memories and feelings sometimes resurface when I'm really stressed.
What have you done in the past to help cope with these emotions?
In the past, I've tried to distract myself with work or hobbies when things get really intense. I've also tried talking to therapists about it, though it's been tricky sticking with it.
I can understand that and we can help proviude the right fit for a therapist if thathelps as well
That could be helpful. Finding someone I can connect with and trust might make a difference.
Do you feel supported by friends and family? Who is your support system?

To be honest, I feel like my support system is pretty limited. I've had some turbulent relationships with friends and family, so I often feel misunderstood or disconnected. It can be tough to rely on others when I don't feel fully supported.
I am sorry you have felt this way. It can be challenging but I am here to help and be a listening ear
Thank you for that. It helps to know there's support here, even when it feels like I'm on my own otherwise.
What do you do for wrok?
I'm a freelance graphic designer. The flexibility can be nice, but the uncertainty and isolation make things tough sometimes.
Have you ever thought of changing your job to something more stable?

Yeah, I've thought about it. The idea of having a more stable job is appealing, but it's hard to make that change because I'm used to the flexibility of freelancing, even if it comes with its own set of challenges.

I completely understand that but at times it can be beneficial to have a rountine and have your feet on the ground. You can also find a job that is able to see accomdate your needs and give you flexibity with your freelancing
That makes sense. Having some stability could really help. Balancing both might be a good way to have some security while still keeping some of the flexibility I'm used to. I'll give it some thought.
Have you been eating okay? at times stress can change things with our bodies
My appetite hasn't really changed much. I guess it varies with how my mood is. On some days, I might not feel like eating much, and on others, it's normal. It just depends on the day.
Do you have any family histroy of mental health diagnosis

Yes, my mother has a history of major depressive disorder, and my aunt was diagnosed with bipolar disorder. My father passed away by suicide when I was a child. There's no documented history of personality disorders, though there have been some relational difficulties in the family.
Have you had any personal mental health disgnosis?
I haven't had a specific diagnosis before, but I did receive treatment for depression in the past. It was mentioned that my relationships seemed quite complex.
In the past was there anything that helped and didn't help with your depression?

I remember that therapy helped me at times, especially when I could talk things out with someone I trusted. However, sticking to treatment was a challenge, especially if I felt dismissed or misunderstood.

It sounds the therapist maybe wasnt a good fit and that can happen. It is important though to try to find someone that hears you and it is a safe space so you can feel motivated to keep going. No one should make you feel dismissed

You're right. Finding the right therapist really matters. It's just hard to keep looking when things don't click, but I'm willing to give it another shot with some help finding someone who fits better.

Ok my plan right now is to give your resources for a new threrapist and i would like to follow up within the next 4-6 weeks after this appoitnment to see if therapy has helped. Please know you are welcomed to reach out and contact me earlier if you think this plan needs to be adjusted. Does this plan sound okay?
That sounds like a good plan to me. I'm willing to give it a try, and I'll reach out if things need adjusting. Thanks for helping me get started on this.

transcript.message: I would like to know a little bit more about how this has been kind of affecting your your personal life and your social life for example uh your life at home with your. Roommates or maybe other friendships, relationships with your family. Has it gotten in the way of that?
Yeah, I've definitely pulled away from people—I don't go out as much, and I feel kind of isolated from my friends and roommates.

Yeah, that's a very difficult feeling. And you mentioned that this has also been going on for a year. To this kind of year long history of you feeling this sense of worry. Has it occurred previously in your life or is this the first time that this has happened?
This is the first time it's been this bad or lasted this long. Before, I had stress, but nothing like this.
Hm okay okay. Got it um uh, I would like to ask you a few more questions about how you're doing right now um. And kind of less related to your previous symptoms. Would that be okay?
Yeah, that's fine, go ahead and ask.
Could you describe your mood for me um lately like what, how have your spirits been?
Honestly, I've just felt pretty on edge and worried most of the time, not really relaxed or happy lately.
Would you say you've been troubled by sadness?
Not really sad, just more anxious and restless than anything else.
Okay yeah yeah, I understand um and aside from this kind of general worry that you've been experiencing. Do you ever experience periods of feeling panicked?
No, I don't really get panic attacks—it's more just this constant anxiety, not big rushes of panic.

And then another question that I have to ask, which is a little sensitive, but it's really important we ask it to everyone. Have any thoughts of harming yourself? For others or ending your own life crossed your mind.
No, I haven't had any thoughts like that.
Okay, got it. And has, so you mentioned that you've been having trouble with your sleep. I'm wondering if your appetite has. Changed at all.
My appetite is about the same—it's just the sleep that's really thrown off.
Oh sorry continue please.
Yeah, I just usually have trouble falling asleep, then I wake up feeling tired all day.
Um, and do you have any history of sleep problems that you know of like has anyone ever told you that you have sleep apnea or anything like that?
No, nobody's ever said anything like that to me before, and I haven't had sleep issues until this anxiety started.
And how has your energy levels and your concentration been since you've, you know, been more worried and getting less sleep?
My energy has definitely dropped, and it's way harder to focus at work or when I'm doing things around the house.
Okay, got it um i'd like to ask you some more questions that are specifically related to anxiety symptoms. Is that all right with you?
Yeah, that's fine, go ahead and ask whatever you need to.
Great um have you ever experienced repetitive, unwanted thoughts or felt the need to repeat certain behaviors unnecessarily?
No, I haven't really had those kinds of thoughts or felt like I had to do things over and over.
Okay um do you have any specific fears which you consider irrational?
No, not really—it's more just general worry about everything instead of one specific fear.
And are you troubled by an inability to relax, would you say that goes along with the worry you describe?
Definitely, I find it almost impossible to just unwind or feel calm these days.
Understanding and do you have any history that you're aware of of trauma? So like for example, physical or sexual abuse?
No, I don't have any history like that.
Got it. Thank you for answering those questions. I know sometimes they can be sensitive and a little difficult for sure.
Yeah, I get it. Thanks for being understanding about it.

Yeah, of course. And kind of while we're on the topic of mental health, I know you mentioned that you hadn't experienced, you know, persistent worry like this. Before the past year. Do you have any other history of any emotional or psychiatric illnesses that you're aware of or any substance? Issues.
No, nothing like that. I don't have any history of other mental health issues or substance problems.
Got it.
Alright, let me know if you need anything else from me.
I think that sums it up mostly. Is there anything else that you wanted to share about what you've been experiencing or any questions that you have?
Yeah, I guess I just want to know—how do you know for sure this is just anxiety and not something physical?

Well, we certainly can rule out certain things that can contribute to symptoms that are, that can manifest like anxiety that are. Different from you know just a psychiatric like illness of a generalized anxiety for example um so we can certainly. Run some tests for common things that would rule it out but I would say that the the duration that you've been experiencing your symptoms. As well as the way you characterize them does sound quite like a generalized anxiety picture that we commonly see.
Okay, I get that, but what kind of tests do people usually do to check for other causes?

Well, for example, you mentioned the the sleep disturbances so so we could do a sleep study. It does sound though more like you're having. That's keeping you up at night rather than problems with getting actual restful sleep. But we could do a sleep study, for example. We could also do some blood work to look for, you know, rule out things that could be causing lower energy like we could make. Make sure that you're not anemic or hypothyroid, for example.
That makes sense. If the blood work and all that come back normal, I guess that would make it clearer this is anxiety, right?

Yeah, and the other way that we diagnose it is we use, you know, diagnostic criteria to help us, help us paint a picture. So whenever. We're you know seeing someone for for an issue that's potentially psychological or psychiatric in nature we really look at everything there. Experiencing a very holistic picture and we kind of compare that against all of our criteria to kind of ascertain what is the. Likely diagnosis and if it's not that, what else could it be? But what you are describing sounds quite a lot like generalized anxiety. With the constant worry about minor and large life events, which is now starting to interfere with your with your day to day and your social life as well.
Okay, got it. I just appreciate hearing a real explanation, so thank you—helps me feel a little more confident in what's going on.
Yeah, i'm glad to hear that um did you have any other questions for me before I leave the room and go speak with my preceptor who's overseeing me today?
No, I think you've answered my main questions. I'll wait to hear what the next steps are from you and your team.
Okay great we'll be back shortly. All right.
Sounds good, thanks for letting me know.

transcript.message: Hi, I'm Angela. I'm a licensed mental health counselor. We talked briefly on the phone last week and I'm really glad that you are able to come to today's appointment.
Hi Angela, I'm James Knight. Thanks for seeing me today. I guess I'm here because things have been pretty up and down for me lately.

Yes, I remember from our conversation that your life has been really challenging lately. Before we get started, I just want to make sure you know about a few confidentiality guidelines. Your information that you share with me is private. If we are going to bill your insurance, I will need to give them some basic information about your diagnoses and treatment plan. The other exceptions to confidentiality would be if you were to tell me that you are going to harm or kill yourself or someone else. Or if you let me know about a child, elder or person who is disabled being abused. Does all of that make sense from your perspective?
Yeah, that makes sense. I appreciate you going over that. I've had experiences where I've felt misunderstood or my feelings were minimized, so it's important to me that things are clear between us.
Yes, I agree. It's important that you feel like this can be a place for you to be open about your thoughts and feelings, and that you can feel understood.
I hope so. It's been tough lately with all these intense mood swings and feeling kind of empty. It's hard when I feel like people just don't get it.
Is it ok with you if I ask you some questions to see if I can better understand what you are going through?
Sure, that's fine. What do you want to know?
Can you describe the mood swings to me? Like what seems to set them off and how long they last?

They can change really quickly. Sometimes it's stuff like feeling ignored or dismissed by someone close to me. I can feel really sad or angry, like everything's crashing down, and it can last hours or even all day.

Ok, yes, I can see how feeling ignored or dismissed would lead you to feel sad or angry. And it sounds like it's sometimes long lasting and sometimes goes on for shorter periods of time. When you say you feel empty, can you tell me more about that feeling?
It’s like there’s nothing there, no purpose or direction. Just this void. It gets overwhelming and hard to shake off.
That sounds like a terrible feeling
Yeah, it really is. It's frustrating and makes everything feel pointless.
Do you struggle with feeling like you should end your life or harm yourself?
I don't feel that way right now. I've struggled with it in the past, but not currently.
Do you remember the last time you felt like killing yourself?
It was a while ago. Things have been rough, but not to that point lately.
Got it. How about wanting to harm yourself in some way that wouldn't kill you, though would cause you bodily harm?
No, I haven't felt that urge lately either.
Ok, thanks for clarifying that. Can you tell me more about your close relationships?
They've been pretty rocky. I seem to idealize people one moment and get really upset with them the next. It makes things hard to keep stable.
Yes, I know what you mean. So sometimes you can feel really good about someone and then something happens where you ten feel really badly about them?
Exactly, it's like a switch flips. It feels out of my control sometimes.
Right, I bet it does.  Do you feel worried about  being rejected or abandoned by people?
Yeah, a lot. It's like I'm always on edge, worrying that people will leave or forget about me.
That can cause a lot of suffering
It really does. It tends to make everything else feel even more unstable.
When you talk about feeling unstable, do you feel like that extends to your identity within yourself too? Like you don't fully know who you are as a person?
Yeah, sometimes I feel like I don't really know myself or where I fit in. It's like everything is shifting around inside.
Yes, I talk with other people who describe that same kind of feeling. Do you struggle with impulsivity in your life like with spending money or sex or anything like that?
I have in the past. I try to keep it in check, but when emotions are high, it can be hard to manage.
Right, when emotions feel out of control, sometimes people turn to things that aren't as healthy
Exactly. It's like looking for any way to feel better, even if it doesn't really help in the long run.
Back to emotions, when you are having the mood swings, do you ever feel like anger is difficult ti manage or control?
Definitely. Anger can be intense, and it's hard to keep it in check, especially when I feel misunderstood.
Yes, I think that anger can be an underdstandable emotion in reaction to feeling misunderstood.  Do you ever have periods of feeling paranoid, like especially when stress is high?
Yeah, sometimes I worry that people are talking about me or plotting against me, especially when things get stressful.
Got it. Yes, I can see how that can happen. How about this symptom - do you ever feel like your body is here but your mind is someplace else? We refer to it as "dissociation"
Yeah, I've had moments like that, especially when things feel really overwhelming. It's like I'm not fully present.
Yes, makes sense. When you are feeling desperate to feel better, do you ever turn to alcohol or drugs in an effort to feel differently?
I used to in my younger days, but not so much now. I try to avoid it.
That's great, what a good decision you are making for yourself.  Sounds like you try to avoid it as much as possible. How often would you say you use alcohol or drugs?
These days, not often at all. I might have a drink occasionally, but I try to keep it in moderation.
Ok, so not a current issue. Would you say that you are having trouble with anxiety?
Yeah, anxiety is definitely something I struggle with, especially around relationships and work stuff.
Is it to the extent that you are not able to function at work?
It makes things difficult sometimes, but I’m still managing to get my work done.

Ok, so it's there, though so far you have been able to continue on with work. And I can appreciate how you would feel anxious around relationships given what you shared earlier about what happens in your relationships.
Yeah, it all seems connected. It just feels like I'm constantly juggling everything and hoping it won't all fall apart.
Just a few more questions about symptoms to make sure I'm not missing anything. Have you been through traumatic events in your lifetime?
Yeah, I've had some tough experiences growing up, especially with my family situation.
Do you find yourself continuing to re-live some of those experiences?
Sometimes memories come back, especially when things get stressful. They can feel pretty vivid.
Sounds really stressful. Do you find yourself actively trying to avoid remembering stressful events?
Yeah, I try not to think about them, but it doesn't always work. They creep in anyway.
How about this - do you notice that your nervous system gets "revved up" and it's difficult to calm yourself? This may interfere with sleep or concentration
Definitely. I often feel on edge, and it makes it hard to relax or focus, especially when I’m stressed.

Ok. I think you've done a really great job today answering a lot of questions and helping me to understand what you are struggling with.  I believe that there are some treatment approaches that we can work with to help reduce these symptoms and your suffering. It will involve meeting regularly and a willingness on your part to do some between session work. What do you think about this?
I appreciate you saying that. I'm willing to try, but I'm a bit nervous about how it will all go. I've had experiences before that didn't always feel helpful.

Yes, I'm hopeful that we can keep open communication so that you can let me know when something is not feeling helpful or you are struggling in some way with our work. I will rely on you for this feedback because I won't be able to automatically know what is happening for you internally
I can do that. I'll try to be open so we can make this work. I just hope things can finally start feeling a little more stable.
Yes, I hear that stability is a major goal that you have - with your emotions, your sense of self and your relationships
Exactly. It would mean a lot to feel like things aren't constantly in chaos.

Right, most people can't really thrive in constant chaos. Ok, so let's wrap up for today and if you're willing, it would be great if you could spend some time between now and next week writing out some goals in your own words for what you want to see different in your life and then we can create a plan
That sounds doable. I'll give it a shot and see what I can come up with. See you next week, then?
Yes, see you next week.
Alright, take care until then.

Honestly, I've just felt pretty on edge and worried most of the time, not really relaxed or happy lately.

Not really sad, just more anxious and restless than anything else.

No, I don't really get panic attacks—it's more just this constant anxiety, not big rushes of panic.

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that.

My appetite is about the same—it's just the sleep that's really thrown off.
Oh sorry continue please.
Yeah, I just usually have trouble falling asleep, then I wake up feeling tired all day.
Um, and do you have any history of sleep problems that you know of like has anyone ever told you that you have sleep apnea or anything like that?
No, nobody's ever said anything like that to me before, and I haven't had sleep issues until this anxiety started.
And how has your energy levels and your concentration been since you've, you know, been more worried and getting less sleep?
My energy has definitely dropped, and it's way harder to focus at work or when I'm doing things around the house.
Okay, got it um i'd like to ask you some more questions that are specifically related to anxiety symptoms. Is that all right with you?
Yeah, that's fine, go ahead and ask whatever you need to.
Great um have you ever experienced repetitive, unwanted thoughts or felt the need to repeat certain behaviors unnecessarily?
No, I haven't really had those kinds of thoughts or felt like I had to do things over and over.
Okay um do you have any specific fears which you consider irrational?
No, not really—it's more just general worry about everything instead of one specific fear.
And are you troubled by an inability to relax, would you say that goes along with the worry you describe?
Definitely, I find it almost impossible to just unwind or feel calm these days.
Understanding and do you have any history that you're aware of of trauma? So like for example, physical or sexual abuse?
No, I don't have any history like that.
Got it. Thank you for answering those questions. I know sometimes they can be sensitive and a little difficult for sure.
Yeah, I get it. Thanks for being understanding about it.

Yeah, of course. And kind of while we're on the topic of mental health, I know you mentioned that you hadn't experienced, you know, persistent worry like this. Before the past year. Do you have any other history of any emotional or psychiatric illnesses that you're aware of or any substance? Issues.
No, nothing like that. I don't have any history of other mental health issues or substance problems.
Got it.
Alright, let me know if you need anything else from me.
I think that sums it up mostly. Is there anything else that you wanted to share about what you've been experiencing or any questions that you have?
Yeah, I guess I just want to know—how do you know for sure this is just anxiety and not something physical?

Well, we certainly can rule out certain things that can contribute to symptoms that are, that can manifest like anxiety that are. Different from you know just a psychiatric like illness of a generalized anxiety for example um so we can certainly. Run some tests for common things that would rule it out but I would say that the the duration that you've been experiencing your symptoms. As well as the way you characterize them does sound quite like a generalized anxiety picture that we commonly see.
Okay, I get that, but what kind of tests do people usually do to check for other causes?

Well, for example, you mentioned the the sleep disturbances so so we could do a sleep study. It does sound though more like you're having. That's keeping you up at night rather than problems with getting actual restful sleep. But we could do a sleep study, for example. We could also do some blood work to look for, you know, rule out things that could be causing lower energy like we could make. Make sure that you're not anemic or hypothyroid, for example.
That makes sense. If the blood work and all that come back normal, I guess that would make it clearer this is anxiety, right?

Yeah, and the other way that we diagnose it is we use, you know, diagnostic criteria to help us, help us paint a picture. So whenever. We're you know seeing someone for for an issue that's potentially psychological or psychiatric in nature we really look at everything there. Experiencing a very holistic picture and we kind of compare that against all of our criteria to kind of ascertain what is the. Likely diagnosis and if it's not that, what else could it be? But what you are describing sounds quite a lot like generalized anxiety. With the constant worry about minor and large life events, which is now starting to interfere with your with your day to day and your social life as well.
Okay, got it. I just appreciate hearing a real explanation, so thank you—helps me feel a little more confident in what's going on.
Yeah, i'm glad to hear that um did you have any other questions for me before I leave the room and go speak with my preceptor who's overseeing me today?
No, I think you've answered my main questions. I'll wait to hear what the next steps are from you and your team.
Okay great we'll be back shortly. All right.
Sounds good, thanks for letting me know.
